description: Every one of the fifteen definitions carries two exemplars -- one document-style, one conversational -- and none of them is extracted. The specification states that exemplars are part of the required shape of a definition, and codebook evidence in the same document says concretely-described features outperform interpretive ones. A consumer retrieving a definition without its exemplars gets the half that measured worse.

Several pairwise separations are grouped into a single unit covering six boundaries at once. Each is independently applicable and independently citable -- a rater resolving observation versus event does not want the formula/definition rule in the same record. The grouping trades retrievability for compactness in the one section the document says is the bulk of a working codebook.
excerpt: | `event` / `decision` | Was a choice made? An event happened to you; a decision was chosen and constrains later action. |

description: The `background`/`event` separation is not extracted at all. It carries its own measurement (13 rater-pairs) and an unusual instruction -- decide from the surrounding context rather than the sentence alone -- which contradicts the surface-test principle the rest of the codebook is built on and is therefore worth recording explicitly.
excerpt: Decide from the surrounding context, not the sentence alone.

description: The `procedure`/`definition` rule and its measurement (15 rater-pairs, all on one naming-convention statement) is absent, as is its discriminating question: does the sentence describe what a thing is, or what to do with it. A naming scheme or set of valid values is a definition even when following it requires action.
excerpt: A naming scheme, a schema, a set of valid values is a `definition` even when following it requires action.

description: The `procedure`/`principle` rule states that where a sentence carries both, the instruction wins -- unless it is hedged or reassuring. That exception is what links it to the reassurance-marker rule, and the link is lost when the two are extracted separately or, as here, one is omitted.
excerpt: Where a sentence carries both, the instruction wins — unless it is hedged or reassuring

description: The classification record's own shape -- the JSON with statement_sha256, tests, tests_fired, multi_fire, and the three version stamps -- is described only indirectly through units about individual fields. The output contract is what a consumer integrates against and it is not represented as a unit in its own right.

Section 2.8's finding that `event` has not been exercised by three consecutive item sets (2 of 608 assignments, background zero across 152 items) is absent. It is a measured statement about coverage that qualifies every reliability figure for those labels, and the document's own reading of it -- untested, not disproven -- is a distinction worth keeping.
excerpt: **`event` has not been exercised by three consecutive item sets**
